newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-CHAPMAN LEADS ENGLISH OPEN AFTER 66.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CHAPMAN LEADS ENGLISH OPEN AFTER 66.

text.p: Englishman Roger Chapman, the European Tour's most celebrated runner-up, shot a faultless six-under-par first round 66 to lead the English Open on Thursday.
The 38-year-old Chapman, who has employed a new sports psychologist to help him overcome "winner's nerves", has never won in 16 years of trying on the European Tour.
He has been a runner-up six times on the Tour and led this event in 1991 until two late bogeys ended his bid.
"That's been the story often," said Chapman. "Now I feel I can enjoy the closing stretch for the first time in my life, so I'm hopeful of my first win."
Chapman, who captured three birdies in five holes after the turn, led by a stroke from Thomas Goegele of Germany. Goegele collected three birdies in his final four holes.
"All of us from my country who play golf are inspired by Bernhard Langer's comeback to win the last two Tour events," said Goegele.

Jose Maria Olazabal, seeking a win to virtually assure himself a Ryder Cup place after only seven counting events since coming back from an 18-month injury layoff, finished three off the pace despite a poor driving round.
His first metal driver, a Makser made by his own company, frequently let him down.

"To win I've got to hit the ball better off the tee," said the 31-year-old Spaniard. "The rest of my game is okay but I'm beginning to believe there isn't a driver in the world which can make me hit the ball straight off the tee."
Englishman Paul Curry holed in one with a four iron at the 187-yard par fourth -- the third ace of his pro career. He shot a 71.
